mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate above 6.0% within the last month signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 6.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in consumer spending (RSAFS) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals a deepening economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both RSAFS and INDPRO decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1.7 million units signals strong consumer confidence and robust economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods during late-cycle expansion when HOUST exceeds 1.7 million, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past month indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 0.5% within the last month signals an impending monetary tightening that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a tight labor market with aggressive monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to rising interest rates and recession fears.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with labor market tightness
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During post-shock recovery, a sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105.0 signals a rebound in manufacturing activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate stronger economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods during post-shock recovery when INDPRO exceeds 105.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.
